body.en:
Three people have died after a fire at a building in London , the London fire brigade (LFB) has said.

The fire service said it received reports of the blaze in New Zealand Way in White City, west London, at 6.52pm on Saturday.

Three men were rescued from a single-storey building by firefighters and treated at the scene by paramedics close to Loftus Road, Queens Park Rangers ground.

Two were declared dead at the scene and another died later in hospital, LFB said.

LFB assistant commissioner Pat Goulbourne said the cause of the blaze is under investigation by its specialist fire investigation officers and the Metropolitan police.

He said: “The fire involved a single-storey pavilion, with just over half of the structure damaged by the fire.”

Goulbourne added: “Control officers mobilised crews from North Kensington, Acton, Chiswick and surrounding fire stations to the scene.

title.en: Israeli strikes kill six people in Gaza including Al Jazeera cameraman, officials say

body.en:
Israeli strikes in Gaza have killed at least six people, including an Al Jazeera cameraman and at least one child, according to health officials and rescuers.

Al Jazeera said it "strongly condemns the heinous crime of targeting and killing" of its correspondent Ahmed Wishah, who was killed in a strike on a central Gaza home on Saturday.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) accused Wishah of being "a terrorist in Hamas' military wing who served as a sniper operative".

Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures the UN regards as reliable, says the Israeli military has killed 1,007 people since a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas came into effect last October.

Al Jazeera said Wishah's death on Saturday "constitutes a new and flagrant violation of all international laws and norms, and reflects a continued systematic policy of targeting journalists and silencing the voice of truth".

The IDF said that Wishah in recent months had advanced sniper attack plans against Israeli troops, without providing evidence.

Two other people were killed along with Wishah in the strike on the home in Bureij refugee camp, according to a local hospital and the Hamas-run civil defence agency, which conducts rescue operations. The IDF also accused the two others killed of being a part of Hamas.

Wishah's brother Mohamed, who was also a correspondent for Al Jazeera, was killed in an Israeli strike in April. The IDF accused him of working in Hamas rocket and weapons production headquarters, without further details.

Meanwhile in the Sabra neighbourhood of Gaza City, four family members were killed in an overnight strike on a home, according to the civil defence, relatives and a nearby hospital.

Shifa Hospital told news agencies that it had received the bodies of the family, including two children. Medics told Reuters that the dead from this strike included two women and a child.

Relative Nael Safadi, who told AFP that the strike hit around 02:00 local time, said his cousins "have no connection to Hamas, nor are they involved in anything. They're just innocent children".

"Is this really a ceasefire?" another cousin, Mohammad Safadi, asked the AP. "We are civilians. I never held a weapon."

Both Israel and Palestinian armed group Hamas have accused one another of violating the ceasefire since October.

title.en: Iran says it has closed Strait of Hormuz over Israeli attacks in Lebanon
title.zh: 伊朗称因以色列袭击黎巴嫩而关闭霍尔木兹海峡

summary.en: Iran claimed to have closed the Strait of Hormuz following Israeli attacks on Lebanon, a claim disputed by the US military. This development occurs just before scheduled talks between the US and Iran in Switzerland.
summary.zh: 伊朗声称因以色列袭击黎巴嫩而关闭霍尔木兹海峡，但美国军方对此说法提出异议。这一事件发生在美国与伊朗在瑞士举行会谈之前。

body.en:
The Iranian military says it has closed the Strait of Hormuz again over Israel's attacks on southern Lebanon - although the US military has disputed the claim.

Iran said deadly Israeli strikes in Lebanon were a breach of Tehran's agreement with the US to end the war.

The US-Iran deal includes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz - a shipping channel through which about 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas passes.

After Iran's statement, a US Central Command spokesperson, Tim Hawkins, told media outlets that "traffic continues to flow", with US forces "monitoring the situation to ensure this remains the case" and that "Iran does not control the Strait of Hormuz".

Later on Saturday, US Vice-President JD Vance departed Washington for direct US-Iran talks in Switzerland on Sunday.

He told reporters he hoped to make progress "on the nuclear issue" and on the "Lebanon ceasefire issue".

Asked about clashes between Israel and Hezbollah and Israeli air strikes in southern Lebanon, Vance said: "Things are actually getting better there, and things are slowing down a little bit."

"It's going to be something we're just going to have to continuously manage to ensure that Israel and Lebanon are both safe and secure. That's fundamentally the goal of this, to make the whole region safe and secure," he said.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said his country would be "demanding that the other side fulfil its commitments".

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will attend the start of the talks, his office told the BBC. Pakistan has acted as a mediator throughout the war, and hosted a previous round of negotiations between the US and Iran in its capital, Islamabad, in April.

Earlier this week the US and Iranian presidents signed an initial agreement aiming to end the war, including in Lebanon, with immediate effect. It includes a commitment to further talks to reach a final deal over the next 60 days.

On Saturday Donald Trump posted on social media that the US could impose its own tolls on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz if the US and Iran did not reach a negotiated deal.

Justifying its announcement that it was closing the strait, the Iranian military accused the US of violating the US-Iran deal by not implementing the first clause of their 14-point memorandum of understanding , which agrees to "the immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including in Lebanon".

Tracking data monitored by BBC Verify suggested that at least five tankers passed through the Strait on Saturday while several vessels appeared to have made U-turns in the area. However earlier on Saturday Centcom said commercial ship traffic through the strait had increased on Saturday, with 55 merchant ships transiting.

title.en: Terror police probe suspected anti-Muslim attacks in Edinburgh
title.zh: 恐怖警察调查爱丁堡涉嫌反穆斯林袭击事件

summary.en: Counterterrorism police have taken charge after a series of violent attacks in the Scottish capital that left five men injured.

body.en:
Counterterrorism police have taken charge after a series of violent attacks in the Scottish capital that left five men injured.

Counterterrorism police have taken over an investigation into suspected anti-Muslim violence in Edinburgh, Scotland , that left five men injured, authorities said Saturday.

The unrest comes as the United Kingdom  is seeing a wave of anti-migrant and anti-Muslim sentiment, including recent riots in Northern Ireland and England .

Emergency services responded late Friday to reports of "violent attacks including threats, robbery and vandalism" across the city, according to a police statement.

Local media reported the attacks began near a mosque before spreading to other areas of the city.

Footage posted to social media appeared to show a shirtless man walking along a street carrying a long weapon.

Another video seemed to show the same man being held on the ground by a police officer and shouting about "protecting the country" from Muslims.

Police said five people — two aged 22 and three others aged 24, 27, and 39 — sustained injuries.

Three of the victims required hospital treatment, but none of the injuries were life-threatening, police said.

A 36-year-old Scottish man was arrested, and authorities said there was no further threat to the public.

"Counter Terrorism Policing Scotland is investigating, supported by other specialist colleagues and local policing officers," the statement said.

The anti-Islamophobia non-profit MEND said several of the victims were Muslims and urged police to "treat this as what the evidence indicates: Islamophobic, far-right terror."

Scotland's First Minister John Swinney said he was "deeply concerned" by the incidents.

Assistant Chief Constable Catriona Paton called for calm, saying "there is no place for racism or faith-based hate in Scotland." The incident follows a broader pattern of unrest across the UK, where tensions over immigration and multiculturalism remain elevated. Critics say far-right groups have been stoking anti-migrant and anti-Muslim sentiment in recent months.

Last week, Belfast saw two nights of serious disorder after a brutal knife attack on a local man.

Video of the incident, allegedly carried out by a Sudanese asylum seeker, spread rapidly online and triggered protests that escalated into violence, with homes and vehicles set on fire.

The week before, protesters clashed with police in Southampton, southern England, over the handling of the murder of 18-year-old student Henry Nowak, who was fatally stabbed by a British Sikh man.

title.en: Are Ukraine drones really exposing gaps in Russia's defense?
title.zh: 乌克兰无人机真的暴露了俄罗斯防御的漏洞吗？

summary.en: Once seen as almost impenetrable, Russian air defenses are now under growing strain from Ukrainian drones. A recent attack on Moscow has reignited debate over Russian vulnerabilities.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Once seen as almost impenetrable, Russian air defenses are now under growing strain from Ukrainian drones. A recent attack on Moscow has reignited debate over Russian vulnerabilities.

Ukrainian drones appear to be getting better at bypassing Russian air defenses to strike critical infrastructure.

After Ukrainian drones hit locations across Moscow on June 18 — the largest attack since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine — a debate was sparked about holes in the country's defense net . 

A major oil refinery in Moscow, which supplies 40% of the region's fuel, was set alight and production appeared to have halted for several days after the attack. There were also evacuations at Russia's largest airport. Eyewitnesses flooded social media with footage of what looked like failed air defense interceptions of the drones.

"That impression forms among non-specialists, who see a missile fly past a drone without hitting it ,"  Ruslan Leviev, a Russian dissident, military analyst and founder of the investigative group Conflict Intelligence Team, told DW.

Exiled Russian journalist Ivan Filippov tracks pro-Kremlin bloggers and noted their growing alarm that Ukraine had found a gap in Russian defenses .

"They don't want the war to stop — they want a more effective war," Filippov told DW, meaning radical reform of the defense ministry and Russia's military-industrial complex. "But I think they understand perfectly well that these reforms are impossible. So these texts tend to be pessimistic."

Anatoliy Khrapchynskyi, a Ukrainian aviation expert and former air force officer, attributed the breaching of Moscow's air defense on June 18 to a combination of two factors: A systemic degradation of Russia's defense architecture and the technological evolution of Ukraine 's strike capabilities.

Leviev wasn't so sure. His team did not record weakening of Russia's defenses because it actually downed more than 90% of the UAVs over Moscow. But the few that managed to get by Russian air defenses caused substantial damage.

Leviev believes the core issue is quantity. As the scale of attacks is increasing, this challenge is the same for both Russia and Ukraine: Mass drone attacks demand more hardware than any industry can supply.

Russian systems, including the Pantsir-S1, were designed to counter classic, large-scale attackers like cruise missiles, Khrapchynskyi told DW. They were calibrated against highly radar-reflective targets made of metal — but modern drones are often made from composite materials like plastic or plywood. This means those systems  are basically "blind" to small drones.

The sheer size of the Russian territory is a challenge on its own. Building an unbroken "air wall" or a single "dome" is impossible, Leviev said.

title.en: Lebanese turtle conservationist Mona Khalil killed by Israeli strike
title.zh: 黎巴嫩海龟保育人士莫娜·哈利勒在以色列袭击中丧生

summary.en: Mona Khalil, a Lebanese conservationist, died from injuries sustained in an Israeli strike on the beach she had dedicated years to protecting. She had refused to leave the area despite the ongoing conflict.
summary.zh: 黎巴嫩环保主义者莫娜·哈利勒因以色列的袭击而受伤，最终不治身亡。她多年来一直致力于保护这片海滩，并拒绝离开。

body.en:
Lebanese environmental activist Mona Khalil, whose work helped turn a stretch of coastline in southern Lebanon into one of the eastern Mediterranean's most important nesting sites for endangered sea turtles, has died after being wounded in an Israeli strike.

Khalil, 76, was injured when her house on Mansouri beach, near the southern city of Tyre, was hit during Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon two weeks ago.

She died on Friday after several days in hospital, according to a local environmental group.

Her death came as Israeli air strikes intensified across southern Lebanon, raising concerns about renewed violence despite diplomatic efforts to maintain a fragile regional peace.

"She is a deeply committed environmental defender," Hisham Younes, the founder and president of Green Southerners, told the BBC.

"She used to talk about the beach like it was a person. Her bond to the sunset, her bond to the water and the turtles….she was really into conservation, and into the soul, the spirit of conservation."

For more than 25 years, Khalil dedicated herself to protecting endangered loggerhead and green sea turtles that nest along Lebanon's southern coast.

Her conservation work began after what her loved ones described as a life-changing encounter with a turtle laying eggs on Mansouri beach in 1999.

A refugee of the Lebanese civil war, Khalil was living in the Netherlands but had returned to visit her family's seaside home.

After learning that sea turtle populations in Lebanon were under threat, she committed herself to protecting them and later returned permanently to the country.

Fast forward a year to 2000, and she helped establish the Orange House Project, an eco-tourism and conservation initiative overlooking Mansouri beach.

What began as a small guesthouse evolved into a centre for environmental education, wildlife protection and marine research, attracting volunteers and visitors from around the world.

Khalil spent decades monitoring nesting sites, documenting marine life and campaigning against coastal development, pollution and destructive fishing practices.

Her efforts helped secure protected status for parts of the coastline and raised awareness of the threats facing marine ecosystems in Lebanon.

Friends and colleagues said she remained committed to her work despite years of conflict in southern Lebanon.

Her home had previously been damaged during the 2006 war between Israel and Hezbollah, but she refused to leave the beach she had spent years protecting.

"Mona barricaded herself inside her house, receiving no visitors and believing she was safe because she is a civilian," environmental activist and friend of Khalil, Maha Joumaa, told local media.

reflection.en: The tragic death of Mona Khalil, a dedicated conservationist, reminds us of the profound sorrow that conflict inflicts on innocent lives and those who quietly serve creation. In moments of such devastating loss, we remember that Yahweh himself grieves with us, as Jesus wept at the tomb of his friend.
reflection.zh: 环保主义者莫娜·哈利勒的悲惨离世，提醒我们冲突给无辜生命和那些默默服务受造物的人们带来了深切的悲痛。在如此毁灭性的损失面前，我们记得雅伟自己也与我们一同悲伤，正如耶稣在朋友的墓前哭泣一样。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: Tourist dies in Dominican Republic luxury resort fire
title.zh: 多米尼加共和国豪华度假村火灾致一名游客死亡

summary.en: A tourist died and nearly 1,700 people were evacuated after a large fire broke out at the Viva Wyndham Dominicus Beach resort in Bayahibe, a popular Caribbean coastal town in the Dominican Republic.
summary.zh: 多米尼加共和国加勒比海岸热门度假小镇巴亚希贝的Viva Wyndham Dominicus Beach度假村发生大火，一名游客死亡，近1,700人被疏散。

body.en:
A huge fire at a luxury beach resort in the Dominican Republic killed one woman and forced nearly 1,700 guests to be evacuated on Friday.

The woman was a 46-year-old Italian tourist, the DAEH emergency services said in a statement to local media. It added that three people were taken to medical facilities and six others were treated on site.

Drone footage shows how widespread the fire was, with buildings spanning the Viva Wyndham Dominicus Beach in the town of Bayahibe on fire, and thick black smoke billowing into the air.

The cause of the early-morning blaze is not yet known, but an initial investigation found the flames spread quickly due to wind conditions and the flammable thatched roofs on some buildings.

The country's Emergency Operations Center (COE) said the fire had been brought under control and guests had been moved to other hotels.

It added that tourist activities in the town and surrounding area were not affected.

Italian news agency Ansa reported that the Italian ambassador to the Dominican Republic met the deceased woman's husband at the hospital. The embassy is helping around 285 Italian tourists who were staying at the resort or nearby, issuing emergency passports to those whose travel documents were destroyed in the fire and arranging flights home.

Bayahibe, a popular resort town on the Caribbean coast, is known for its clear blue waters and sandy beaches.

Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, which franchises about 8,400 hotels around the world, said in a short statement to the BBC that while "hotel teams safely evacuated guests and staff," one guest died.

"We send our thoughts to the family while we await autopsy results to determine the cause," it said.

It said the hotel, which is independently owned and operated, is closed and will remain so until further notice.
body.zh: 周五，多米尼加共和国一处豪华海滩度假村发生大火，造成一名妇女死亡，近 1,700 名客人被迫疏散。 DAEH 紧急服务部门在给当地媒体的一份声明中称，这名女子是一名 46 岁的意大利游客。声明补充说，三人被送往医疗机构，另外六人在现场接受治疗。 无人机拍摄的画面显示，火灾范围有多广，巴亚希贝镇 Viva Wyndham Dominicus 海滩上的建筑物起火，浓烟滚滚到空中。 凌晨起火的原因尚不清楚，但初步调查发现，由于风力条件和一些建筑物的易燃茅草屋顶，火势迅速蔓延。 该国紧急行动中心（COE）表示，火势已得到控制，客人已被转移到其他酒店。 它补充说，该镇及周边地区的旅游活动没有受到影响。 意大利安莎通讯社报道称，意大利驻多米尼加共和国大使在医院会见了死者的丈夫。大使馆正在帮助住在度假村或附近的约285名意大利游客，为旅行证件在火灾中被毁的游客发放紧急护照，并安排回国航班。 巴亚希贝是加勒比海岸的一个热门度假小镇，以其清澈蔚蓝的海水和沙滩而闻名。 温德姆酒店及度假村在全球拥有约 8,400 家酒店特许经营权，在给 BBC 的一份简短声明中表示，虽然“酒店团队安全疏散了客人和员工”，但仍有一名客人死亡。 声明称：“我们在等待尸检结果以确定死因的同时，将我们的想法传达给死者家属。” 该公司表示，这家独立拥有和经营的酒店已关闭，并将继续关闭，直至另行通知。

reflection.en: News of a resort fire and the loss of life reminds us of how quickly safety can be disrupted and how vulnerable we are to sudden events. In moments of crisis and uncertainty, Yahweh remains our steadfast refuge and strength, a constant help in times of trouble.
reflection.zh: 度假村火灾和生命逝去的消息提醒我们，安全可能瞬间被打破，我们是多么容易受到突发事件的影响。在危机和不确定时刻，雅伟仍然是我们坚定的避难所和力量，是患难中随时的帮助。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: Spain: PM's wife must face corruption trial, judge rules
title.zh: 西班牙：法官裁定首相夫人必须面临腐败审判

summary.en: A court in Madrid has ruled that there is sufficient evidence for the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, Begona Gomez, to face a corruption trial. The 55-year-old university director is currently banned from leaving the country.
summary.zh: 马德里一家法院裁定，有足够证据对首相佩德罗·桑切斯的妻子贝戈尼亚·戈麦斯提起腐败审判。这位55岁的大学主任已被禁止离境。

body.en:
A court in Madrid ruled that there is sufficient evidence against Begona Gomez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. The 55-year-old university director is banned from leaving the country.

The wife of Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has been ordered to stand trial on corruption charges, a court order released on Saturday said.

Begona Gomez is ‌accused of using her position as the head of the government's wife to secure work contracts.

The case is one of several graft cases facing the PM's center-left minority government.

The court in Madrid agreed that there was sufficient evidence to bring Gomez's case to trial in front of a jury.

Investigating judge Juan Carlos Peinado told Gomez to surrender ​her passport, barred her from leaving the country and ordered ​her ‌to report to court twice a month.

The court said "instructions shall be issued to all border posts and civilian and military airports" to ensure Gomez remains on home soil.

Sanchez's ​Socialist PSOE party reacted to the ruling on X, saying: "[Gomez] has been subjected to judicial and political ⁠persecution ​for two years. Today's development is another step ​in that process."

The case began with a complaint filed by Manos Limpias (Clean Hands), a legal pressure group set up by a lawyer with ties to the far right.

An investigation was opened in April 2024 to decide whether Gomez had exploited her position as Sanchez's wife for private gain.

It centers on an academic chair at Madrid’s Complutense University that Gómez co-directed, along with allegations that she used public resources and her connections to advance private business interests.

Gomez was  formally charged in April with embezzlement, influence peddling, corruption in business dealings and misappropriation of funds.

She has denied the allegations, while Sanchez has repeatedly refused to step down and call early elections.

Several senior figures close to Sanchez, including the PSOE's number three and his former transport minister, are also under investigation over alleged kickbacks linked to public works contracts, oil and gas deals and the procurement of COVID-19 masks.

Separately, Spain's High Court is investigating former Prime Minister Jose Luis Rodriguez Zapatero over allegations that he headed a lobbying network which profited from influencing public authorities on behalf of third parties, including the airline Plus Ultra.

The cases threaten to bring down Sanchez's fragile coalition government, which came to power in 2018 promising to clean up Spanish politics after toppling the conservative Popular Party (PP) in a no-confidence vote over its own corruption scandal.

body.zh: 马德里一家法院裁定，有足够的证据对总理佩德罗·桑切斯的妻子贝戈娜·戈麦斯不利。这位 55 岁的大学校长被禁止出境。 周六发布的法院命令称，西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯的妻子已被勒令因腐败指控接受审判。 贝戈纳·戈麦斯被指控利用政府首脑妻子的职位来获取工作合同。 此案是总理中左翼少数政府面临的几起贪污案件之一。 马德里法院同意，有足够的证据将戈麦斯的案件提交陪审团审理。 调查法官胡安·卡洛斯·佩纳多要求戈麦斯交出护照，禁止她离开该国，并命令她每月两次到法庭报到。 法院表示，“应向所有边境哨所以及民用和军用机场发出指示”，以确保戈麦斯留在祖国。 桑切斯领导的社会党 PSOE 对 X 案的裁决做出反应，称：“[戈麦斯]两年来一直受到司法和政治迫害。今天的发展是这一过程中的又一步。” 此案始于马诺斯·林皮亚斯（“干净的手”）提出的投诉，这是一个由与极右翼有联系的律师成立的法律压力团体。 2024 年 4 月展开调查，以确定戈麦斯是否利用桑切斯妻子的地位谋取私利。 它以戈麦斯共同领导的马德里康普顿斯大学的一位学术主席为中心，并指控她利用公共资源和人脉关系来促进私人商业利益。 戈麦斯于四月被正式指控贪污、以权谋私、商业交易中腐败和挪用资金。 她否认了这些指控，而桑切斯则一再拒绝下台并呼吁提前选举。 与桑切斯关系密切的几位高级人物，包括社会工人党的三号人物和他的前交通部长，也因涉嫌与公共工程合同、石油和天然气交易以及采购 COVID-19 口罩有关的回扣而接受调查。 另外，西班牙高等法院正在调查前首相何塞·路易斯·罗德里格斯·萨帕特罗，指控他领导一个游说网络，该网络通过代表第三方（包括 Plus Ultra 航空公司）影响公共当局而获利。 这些案件有可能导致桑切斯脆弱的联合政府垮台，该政府于 2018 年上台，在就自身腐败丑闻进行的不信任投票中推翻了保守的人民党 (PP) 后，承诺整顿西班牙政治。 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果...

reflection.en: This news reminds us of the universal call to integrity, especially for those connected to public life. Yahweh asks us to pursue justice and walk humbly, principles that guide all individuals, regardless of their position. May this process uphold fairness and truth for all involved.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻提醒我们，所有人，特别是与公共生活相关的人，都应秉持正直。雅伟要求我们行公义，存谦卑的心与他同行，这些原则指引着每个人，无论其地位如何。愿这一过程能为所有相关方维护公平和真相。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: BBC sees destroyed villages in Israeli-occupied southern Lebanon
title.zh: BBC 看到以色列占领的黎巴嫩南部村庄被毁

summary.en: Travelling with a humanitarian convoy, BBC's Hugo Bachega has been given rare access to a part of Lebanon under Israeli occupation.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The BBC has been given rare access to the part of southern Lebanon that is under Israeli occupation, as part of a humanitarian convoy of the Order of Malta distributing aid to Christian villages that have been isolated because of the war.

The mission happened on Thursday, a day before the announcement of a new ceasefire in the conflict between Israel and the Shia Muslim armed group Hezbollah. The team saw the Israeli military presence but was not allowed to film much of the journey.

Israel says it has no intention of withdrawing its troops from Lebanon, and that its plan is to create a security zone along the border, Hezbollah-free, to protect its northern communities from the group's rockets and drones.

In the occupied areas, mainly Shia villages have been completely destroyed by Israeli air strikes or demolitions. Human rights groups say that some of what has happened there amounts to the deliberate destruction of civilian infrastructure, a possible war crime.

The BBC's Middle East correspondent Hugo Bachega and video journalist Neha Sharma report from southern Lebanon.

The BBC’s Shaimaa Khalil was outside the Iran v New Zealand opening round match as protesters called for an end to Tehran’s clerical regime.

It's not clear if the deal means the Israelis will pause their offensive in Lebanon, BBC international editor Jeremy Bowen reports.

In a call with the US president, the BBC’s Sarah Smith asked Trump about the war in Iran and his relationship with the Israeli leader.

One person was killed and more than 60 injured in the Iranian drone strike on Wednesday.

BBC’s Sarah Smith looks at why both countries are in a tense cycle of negotiations, despite the progress President Trump consistently claims.

Iranian authorities have imposed an internet ban but using trusted sources, special correspondent Fergal Keane hears from those traumatised by conflict and government repression.

Thousands of people have taken part in the Palestine Marathon, which returns to Bethlehem after a two-year pause over the Gaza War.

President Trump has suspended anoperation to guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz - BBC Verify explains the timeline.

Capt Raman Kapoor's ship is one of several to be stranded in the strait in the midst of the power struggle between the US and Iran.

The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is quitting oil cartel Opec after nearly 60 years of membership.

The US president says he saved eight Iranian women from execution, but Iran says otherwise.

The 300 couples were selected in a draw of nearly 2,000 people to be a part of the joint celebration.

The US and Iran's rival blockades of the Strait of Hormuz have become a "test of wills", says Lyse Doucet.

body.zh: 作为马耳他骑士团人道主义车队的一部分，英国广播公司获得了难得的机会进入以色列占领下的黎巴嫩南部地区，向因战争而孤立的基督教村庄分发援助物资。 这次任务发生在星期四，就在以色列和什叶派穆斯林武装组织真主党之间的冲突宣布新停火的前一天。该团队看到了以色列军队的存在，但不被允许拍摄大部分旅程。 以色列表示无意从黎巴嫩撤军，并计划沿边境建立一个没有真主党的安全区，以保护其北部社区免受真主党火箭弹和无人机的袭击。 在被占领地区，主要是什叶派村庄被以色列空袭或拆除完全摧毁。人权组织表示，那里发生的一些事情相当于故意破坏民用基础设施，可能构成战争罪。 BBC 中东记者雨果·巴切加 (Hugo Bachega) 和视频记者内哈·夏尔马 (Neha Sharma) 从黎巴嫩南部进行报道。 英国广播公司 (BBC) 的沙伊玛·哈利勒 (Shaimaa Khalil) 在伊朗对阵新西兰的首轮比赛外，抗议者呼吁结束德黑兰的教权政权。 据英国广播公司国际编辑杰里米·鲍文报道，目前尚不清楚该协议是否意味着以色列将暂停对黎巴嫩的攻势。 在与美国总统的通话中，英国广播公司的莎拉·史密斯向特朗普询问了伊朗战争以及他与以色列领导人的关系。 周三，伊朗无人机袭击造成 1 人死亡、60 多人受伤。 英国广播公司 (BBC) 的莎拉·史密斯 (Sarah Smith) 探讨了为什么尽管特朗普总统一直声称取得了进展，但两国仍处于紧张的谈判周期。 伊朗当局实施了互联网禁令，但特约记者费格尔·基恩通过可信来源听取了那些因冲突和政府镇压而受到创伤的人的消息。 数千人参加了巴勒斯坦马拉松比赛，该赛事在因加沙战争而暂停两年后重返伯利恒。 特朗普总统已暂停引导船只通过霍尔木兹海峡的行动 - BBC verify 解释了时间表。 拉曼·卡普尔船长的船是在美国和伊朗之间的权力斗争中滞留在海峡的几艘船之一。 阿拉伯联合酋长国 (UAE) 在成为欧佩克成员国近 60 年后，即将退出石油卡特尔组织。 美国总统称他拯救了八名伊朗妇女免遭处决，但伊朗却另有说法。 近 2,000 人参与抽签，最终选出 300 对情侣参加联合庆祝活动。 杜赛特表示，美国和伊朗对霍尔木兹海峡的相互封锁已经成为“意志的考验”。 分析表明，视频的部分内容似乎是在船舶航行数小时后拍摄的……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到对脆弱群体的怜悯。Galatians 6:2提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以具体的怜悯与接纳来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: Zelenskyy returns Poland's highest honor as row deepens
title.zh: 随着争执加深，泽连斯基归还波兰最高荣誉

summary.en: Ukraine's president has returned a medal to Poland after a decision to strip him of the honor. Warsaw has been one of Kyiv's key allies since Russia's war in Ukraine.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Ukraine's president has returned a medal to Poland after a decision to strip him of the honor. Warsaw has been one of Kyiv's key allies since Russia's war in Ukraine.

Top Ukrainian officials, including President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said on Saturday that they were returning Polish state honors after Polish President Karol Nawrocki stripped the Ukrainian president of Poland's highest award.

Zelenskyy said in a social media post that sent back the Order of the White Eagle, which he received in 2023 as a symbol of friendship between Poland and Ukraine.

"Ukraine will remain open to all meaningful formats of interaction with Poland, in order to strive to avoid misinterpretations of the complex and painful pages of the past of our peoples and to ensure due respect for all innocent victims of the 20th century," he wrote.

He called the medal a symbol of Poland's "highest trust," but also suggested it no longer held the same meaning after Nawrocki's decision. 

The Polish decision to strip the honor from Zelenskyy could further strain ties between the two close strategic partners as Kyiv seeks to rally international support to pressure Russia to end its war in Ukraine .

"This is a gift to the Moscow aggressor, who will certainly use it against both of our countries," Zelenskyy's chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, wrote on social media, saying that he was returning the Gold Officer's Cross of the Polish Order of Merit. 

On Friday, Nawrocki announced that Zelenskyy would be stripped of the Order of the White Eagle — Poland's highest state honor, which had been awarded by former President Andrzej Duda in 2023.

The decision followed Zelenskyy's move to name a military unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) ,  a World War II militia that Warsaw accuses of participating in massacres of Poles.

Poland has been one of Ukraine's key allies since Russia's full-scale invasion, hosting hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian refugees.

Nawrocki said the move would not affect Poland's support for Ukraine's defense against Russia. 

Ukraine's ambassador to Warsaw, Vasyl Bodnar, described the move "as a gesture towards all the Ukrainian people" and announced that he was relinquishing his Knight's Cross of the Polish Order of Merit.

Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga also said that he would return a Polish award he received in 2022, calling the decision "a strategic mistake … that benefits only Moscow."

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk , a political rival of Nawrocki, urged both countries to preserve their solidarity, warning that a dispute between Poland and Ukraine "delights Putin and shocks our allies."

title.en: One killed and dozens hurt in train collision north of London
title.zh: 伦敦北部发生火车相撞事故，造成一人死亡数十人受伤

summary.en: A train collision north of London resulted in one fatality and dozens of injuries. Social media footage depicted the front of one train entangled with the rear of another.
summary.zh: 伦敦北部发生火车相撞事故，造成一人死亡，数十人受伤。社交媒体上发布的视频显示，一列火车的车头与另一列火车的车尾缠绕在一起。

body.en:
A train driver has died and dozens more injured in a collision between two commuter services in London on Friday.

Both trains were travelling south to London St Pancras station on Friday afternoon when they collided outside the town of Bedford, about 100km north of London. The trains were travelling from Corby and Nottingham respectively.

East Midlands Railway, which operated both London-bound trains involved in the crash, confirmed in a statement on X on Saturday that the driver of one of the services had been killed. The company had cancelled all trains to and from St Pancras for the rest of Friday and was unable to confirm the schedule for Saturday.

A video posted on social media by one of the passengers showed what appeared to be the front of one train entangled with the back of another, with the carriages appearing to remain upright on the tracks.

The East of England Ambulance Service said that in addition to a person who died at the scene, 11 people suffered very serious injuries, 22 were seriously injured and 56 had minor injuries.

"My thoughts are with the family of the person who has sadly lost their life, and with those who have been seriously injured," Prime Minister Keir Starmer said in a statement.

The cause of the incident was not immediately known, and transport minister Heidi Alexander said an investigation was underway.

Peter Knapp, a doctor who said on social media site Bluesky he was on board one of the trains, described a "sudden crash" with one carriage off the rails and said he had sustained minor injuries.

"There was a moment of being flung into the chair in front, and then I saw smoke," Knapp said.

"I got up and I saw a lot of people who were unable to speak, had broken legs," he said.

"And then I managed to get out of the train and because I'm quite thin I was able to squeeze out through the gap in the doors."

Various posts on social media showed dozens of people, some with bandages but many who appeared uninjured, standing and sitting among emergency vehicles parked on a road that runs parallel to the train tracks.

The RMT union, which represents many railway workers, said it was monitoring the situation and expressed its concern over reports of "serious injuries" suffered by both train staff and passengers.

title.en: Bolivia declares state of emergency over blockade crisis
title.zh: 玻利维亚因封锁危机宣布进入紧急状态

summary.en: Bolivia has declared a state of emergency as roadblocks and demonstrations have intensified since April, severely disrupting the nation.
summary.zh: 玻利维亚宣布进入紧急状态，因为自四月以来，路障和示威活动加剧，严重瘫痪了该国。

body.en:
Bolivia's military is poised to crack down on protesters after President Rodrigo Paz declared a state of emergency following weeks of crippling blockades.

The state of emergency will enable wider military deployment to clear blockades and restore order after protests brought the economy to a halt in the past 50 days.

The emergency declaration on Saturday gives Paz broader constitutional tools to restore order, such as sending armed forces to clear blockades, which have been intensifying since April.

While the order goes into effect immediately, the president must notify Congress of the state of emergency within 24 hours ‌of issuing the ‌decree, which then ⁠has up to 72 hours to approve or reject the measure.

Protesting groups, many allied to former leftist president Evo Morales, have cut off key roads, stranding trucks and choking supplies of food, fuel and medicines to many areas, including La Paz.

The conflict initially erupted after Paz abruptly cut longstanding fuel subsidies to shrink the deficit amid a worsening dollar crunch and talks with the International Monetary Fund.

Despite later steps to stabilise fuel ⁠prices and reverse unpopular land reforms, protests intensified into broader discontent, with ‌unions demanding wage increases, an end to fuel and dollar shortages, and Paz's resignation.

Paz's declaration came in a live message to the ‌nation just hours after he unveiled a deal struck on Friday with the main union, the Bolivian Workers Confederation, that aimed to ease tension.

However, many roads connecting the South American nation's main production centre are under the control of rural associations aligned with Morales, who were not a part of the negotiations and are continuing to protest mainly in the area of Cochabamba.

Paz said the crisis had evolved into an organised attempt to destabilise ‌democracy after weeks of violence and blockades.

He said the state of emergency aims to restore order, protect citizens and ensure the flow of essential goods, while warning that those continuing disruptions would face legal consequences.

"This is not a state of emergency to restrict people's lives ... It is a state of emergency to give freedom back to the people, to free Bolivia from those who use political conflict to block roads and harm the population," Paz said.

summary.en: The patriotic makeover of the historic Lincoln Memorial monument has gone disastrously wrong.

body.en:
Strips of "American-flag blue" paint are rising from the bottom of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, videos circulating online appear to show, in the latest disaster to hit its botched $14.6 million ($20.8M) refurbishment.

The Reflecting Pool, which civil rights activist Martin Luther King Jr. looked over as he gave his famous "I have a dream" speech, has undergone a makeover at the direction of Donald Trump to commemorate the country's 250th birthday on 4 July this year.

In May, the pool was drained and a commercial-grade sealant was reportedly added to its granite bottom.

The Virginia-based Atlantic Industrial Coatings company was awarded a controversial US$13.1 million ($18.7M) no-bid contract for the job after having previously worked on one of Trump's golf courses.

"We did a hell of a job," Trump told reporters at the White House last week upon completion, claiming just US$10 million had been spent.

Company owner Eddie Wood confirmed in an email to US publication NBC that the cost had, in fact, blown out.

"But everybody’s looking at that Reflecting Pool," Trump continued. "They can’t believe it reflects. We used a dark blue, it’s called American flag blue."

However, visitors to the iconic Washington site have noticed that the water has turned a distinct shade of green.

Wayne Sobey, environmental consultant at Algae Control Australia, told SBS News that "shallow, flat, non‑circulating pools" like the Lincoln Memorial's create "almost perfect conditions for algal growth," something the administration is continuing to deny is a problem.

Here's how the colour of the Lincoln Reflecting Pool became the latest political flashpoint in a politically charged United States.

Trump's desired overhaul of the Reflecting Pool is part of an ongoing administration push to "beautify" American cities, and its capital in particular, following what it sees as years of Democrat neglect.

Such projects in Washington DC include the complete knock-down and rebuild of the East Wing of the White House, the plans to build a towering victory arch in Washington that will exceed the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, and a US$7.5 million plan to paint the Eisenhower building.

The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is a 619 by 51 metre rectangular pool built in 1922 between the Washington Monument and the Lincoln Memorial.

title.en: Deadly H5 strain of bird flu has been confirmed in Australia — here's what it means

summary.en: Australia has confirmed its first case of the deadly H5N1 avian influenza, a significant development for the nation's public health.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚已确认首例致命H5N1禽流感病例，这对该国的公共卫生而言是一个重大进展。

body.en:
For years, as cases of the deadly H5 strain of bird influenza wreaked havoc among animal populations across the globe, Australia had been the sole continent to avoid it successfully — until now.

On Saturday, the first positive case of the virus on the Australian mainland was confirmed.

Agriculture minister Julie Collins confirmed at a press conference in Canberra that the H5 bird flu was detected in a migratory bird in Western Australia.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Australia will do all it can to curb any spread of H5N1 bird flu.

"There's no evidence of any mass mortalities, and there's no evidence that it's in our poultry or agriculture system at this stage," Collins added.

In its efforts to tackle previous bird-flu outbreaks, Australia has tightened biosecurity measures at farms, tested shore birds for disease, vaccinated vulnerable species, and war-gamed response plans for an H5N1 outbreak.

A single migratory wild seabird potentially infected with the disease was found in Western Australia on 14 June.

Before the suspected positive case was confirmed, Collins said on Friday that it would be "not unexpected" to discover.

"This will be sobering, but not unexpected given the spread globally," she said.

The bird was a brown skua — a sub-Antarctic species — that was found on a remote beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park near Esperance, about 700km southeast of Perth.

WA Agriculture and Food Minister Jackie Jarvis said the bird was isolated after it was discovered in an unwell state on Sunday and died that night.

"I'm told it is not normal for them to be on the south coast of Western Australia," Jarvis said.

"But I am also told it's not uncommon if a bird is sick to actually be sort of blown off course, as it were."

Initial tests were confirmed overnight by the CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness.

Senior lecturer at the Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies at the University of Tasmania, Dr Jane Younger, said the species infected with the virus could give clues to its origin.

"The species involved are important," she said, noting that they are Southern Ocean and sub-Antarctic birds.

This suggests that the virus "probably reached mainland Australia through Southern Ocean wildlife movements, rather than through the northern hemisphere route we have been watching closely," Younger explained.

But, she says, genetic analysis was still essential to identify the virus' origin and whether it was linked to current outbreaks across the Southern Ocean.

reflection.en: The confirmation of a deadly H5 bird flu strain reminds us of life's fragility and the constant presence of illness in our world. In such times, the Scriptures encourage us to pray for those affected by disease and for wisdom for those working to contain it. We can bring our concerns to Yahweh, trusting in His compassion and care.
reflection.zh: 致命H5禽流感病毒株的确认提醒我们生命的脆弱以及疾病在世上的持续存在。在这样的时刻，圣经鼓励我们为受疾病影响的人祷告，也为那些致力于控制疫情的人寻求智慧。我们可以将我们的担忧带到雅伟面前，信靠祂的怜悯和看顾。

verse.textEn: Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them.
verse.textZh: 你们中间有病了的呢，他就该请教会的长老来；他们可以奉主的名用油抹他，为他祷告。

title.en: China Desk
title.zh: 中国观察

strap.en: Policy signals, social change, and national developments inside China.
strap.zh: 聚焦中国内部政策走向、社会变化与国家动态。

title.en: Petrol prices in Australia are now lower than before the Iran war began. Is the oil crisis over and what happens next?
title.zh: 澳大利亚的汽油价格现在低于伊朗战争开始前。石油危机结束了吗？接下来会发生什么？

summary.en: Fuel suppliers outside the Middle East have proved to be much more flexible than analysts expected – and China surprised everyone Australians were warned soon after the Middle East conflict started that the country could run short on fuel, with prices rising to record levels...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Fuel suppliers outside the Middle East have proved to be much more flexible than analysts expected – and China surprised everyone Australians were warned soon after the Middle East conflict started that the country could run short on fuel, with prices rising to record levels owing to disrupted oil supplies. Now, amid an uneasy peace deal and continued supply disruptions, petrol prices are lower than they were before the conflict began and official warnings over fuel usage have largely disappeared. Continue reading...
body.zh: 事实证明，中东以外的燃料供应商比分析师预期的灵活得多，而中国令所有人感到惊讶。中东冲突爆发后不久，澳大利亚人就收到警告称，该国可能出现燃料短缺，由于石油供应中断，价格上涨至创纪录水平。现在，由于和平协议不稳定，供应持续中断，汽油价格低于冲突开始前，官方对燃料使用的警告也基本消失。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Charging ahead: EVs outpace growth predictions
title.zh: 电动汽车：超越增长预期，加速前进

summary.en: Electric vehicles are becoming more affordable, efficient, and capable of longer distances, exceeding initial growth forecasts. China is leading this transition, with Europe and other nations rapidly advancing as well.
summary.zh: 电动汽车正变得更便宜、更高效，续航里程也比以往任何时候都长，其增长速度超出了预期。中国正在推动这一转型，而欧洲和其他国家也正在迅速追赶。

body.zh: 电动汽车变得越来越便宜、越来越高效，而且行驶距离比以往任何时候都更远。中国正在推动这一转型，但欧洲和其他国家正在快速追赶。 全球电动汽车 (EV) 市场的增长速度远远快于预期。短短六年内，销量增长了十倍，到 2025 年，全球电动汽车销量将达到约 2100 万辆。 中国和欧洲处于领先地位，但世界其他地区的市场也在快速增长。 中国长期以来一直在投资太阳能和风能以及电池技术——电动汽车最关键的组成部分。 得益于先进的研究和大规模生产，电动汽车电池成本大幅下降。如今，它们的成本仅为 10 年前的四分之一，而且价格还在继续下降。 中国是世界上最大的汽车市场，消费者正在从政府的产业战略中获益。自 2024 年以来，电动汽车的成本低于内燃机汽车，国家多年来一直在迅速扩大充电基础设施，而且中国的电力非常实惠。 2015年，电动汽车仅占中国新车销量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，这一比例已攀升至 61%。 电动汽车依靠电力运行并通过电缆充电。在全球范围内，三分之二的电动汽车是所谓的电池电动汽车 (BEV)，仅由电力驱动。剩下的三分之一还配备了燃气发动机，用于长途旅行时的备用——这些被称为增程电动汽车 (EREV) 或插电式混合动力电动汽车 (PHEV)。 相比之下，所谓的混合动力电动汽车 (HEV) 始终需要汽油或柴油来为其内燃机提供动力。电动机提供一些帮助，仅通过再生制动产生电力。这项技术在一定程度上降低了城市驾驶的燃油消耗，但混合动力汽车在国际统计中并未被算作电动汽车。 2018年，电动汽车仅占欧盟新车注册量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，售出的新车中近三分之一是电动汽车。 北欧处于领先地位。在挪威，现在销售的几乎所有新车都是电动汽车（99%），其次是丹麦（82%）和瑞典（65%）。该地区各国政府支持气候友好型出行，并正在扩大充电基础设施。 在英国，2026 年 4 月注册的新车中有 39% 是电动汽车，其次是德国（37%）和法国（32%）。在这三个国家，电动汽车销量与去年同月相比都翻了一番。 近年来，美国市场陷入停滞。 2023 年至 2025 年间，电动汽车占...

reflection.en: The rapid advancements in electric vehicle technology, making them cheaper and more efficient, reflect a remarkable acceleration of human knowledge and innovation. This progress reminds us of the human capacity to explore and develop new solutions, continually expanding our understanding and capabilities.
reflection.zh: 电动汽车技术日新月异，变得更便宜、更高效，这反映了人类知识和创新的显著加速。这种进步提醒我们，人类有能力探索和开发新的解决方案，不断拓展我们的理解和能力。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: For women in China frustrated by sexism, female comics are offering a release
title.zh: 在中国，女性喜剧演员为厌倦性别歧视的女性提供宣泄出口

summary.en: Standup comedy in China is providing a platform for women to discuss sensitive topics, including sexism, offering a sense of release and shared experience. Performers, however, remain cautious of censorship limits as they navigate this space in venues like a small performing arts theatre in east Beijing.
summary.zh: 中国的脱口秀喜剧为女性提供了一个平台，让她们可以讨论包括性别歧视在内的敏感话题，从而获得宣泄和共同的体验。然而，表演者们在北京东部一家小型表演艺术剧院等场所进行表演时，仍对审查限制保持警惕。

body.en: Standup comedy gives women a space to talk about certain topics that have become more sensitive, while performers remain wary of censorship limits Packed into the upstairs theatre of a small performing arts space in east Beijing, more than 100 people, mostly women, are giddy with anticipation. “Who did you come to see?” asks the MC, fashionably dressed in a faded denim two-piece suit. The answer is bellowed in unison back to him: “Fang Zhuren!” Fang Shaoli, AKA Director Fang ( Fang Zhuren ), has built a cult following in China in the past two years. Decidedly less fashionable than the evening’s host, Fang is dressed in a yellow hoodie and dark blue jeans. Her everywoman attire is part of the appeal. With a stout frame and short, sensible haircut, Fang, who was born in 1975, hails from rural part of east China’s Shandong province. Before discovering the art of standup comedy she worked in factories and on construction sites, but mainly lived as a housewife to a difficult husband. Her jokes riff on the deep sexism that permeates Chinese culture, particularly away from the big urban centres like Beijing and Shanghai. Continue reading...
body.zh: 单口喜剧为女性提供了谈论某些变得更加敏感的话题的空间，而表演者们仍然对审查制度的限制保持警惕北京东部一个小型表演艺术空间的楼上剧场里，有 100 多人（其中大部分是女性）满怀期待。 “你是来看谁的？”身穿褪色牛仔两件套西装的主持人问道。对方齐声喊道：“方主任！”方绍立，又名方主任（方主任），过去两年在中国建立了一批狂热的追随者。方穿着黄色连帽衫和深蓝色牛仔裤，明显不如当晚主持人时尚。她的普通女性着装是其吸引力的一部分。方出生于1975年，来自中国东部山东省的农村地区，身材魁梧，留着一头漂亮的短发。在发现单口喜剧艺术之前，她曾在工厂和建筑工地工作过，但主要是作为一位难相处的丈夫的家庭主妇生活。她的笑话反复提及了渗透在中国文化中的根深蒂固的性别歧视，尤其是在远离北京和上海等大城市中心的地方。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the human need to express frustrations and experiences, especially when facing societal pressures like sexism. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us of the importance of speaking up for those whose voices are often unheard, advocating for justice and dignity. Even in challenging environments, creative expression can offer a vital space for shared...
reflection.zh: 这个故事突显了人类表达挫折和经历的需求，尤其是在面对性别歧视等社会压力时。箴言31:8-9提醒我们，为那些常常被忽视的声音发声，倡导公义和尊严是何等重要。即使在充满挑战的环境中，创造性的表达也能为共同的理解和释放提供一个重要的空间，这反映了雅伟对边缘群体的关怀。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Border Force officer and Hong Kong trade official jailed for spying for China
title.zh: 英国边境部队官员和香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动被判入狱

summary.en: A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official have been sentenced to 10 and eight years in prison, respectively, after being convicted of spying for China. These are the first convictions under the UK's National Security Act.
summary.zh: 一名英国边境部队官员和一名香港贸易官员因替中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，刑期分别为10年和8年。这是英国根据《国家安全法》首次定罪的案件。

body.en: Peter Wai and Bill Yuen sentenced to 10 and eight years at Old Bailey in first convictions under National Security Act A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong trade official based in London have been jailed for spying for China in the first such conviction in British criminal history. Peter Wai, who conducted “shadow policing” operations on Chinese dissidents in the UK, was sentenced to 10 years, while his handler, Bill Yuen, received an eight-year term. Continue reading...
body.zh: Peter Wai和Bill Yuen根据《国家安全法》首次在老贝利被判刑10年和8年。一名英国边防部队官员和一名驻伦敦的香港贸易官员因为中国从事间谍活动而被判入狱，这是英国犯罪史上的首次此类定罪。在英国对中国持不同政见者进行“影子警察”行动的韦彼得被判处10年徒刑，而他的经纪人袁比尔则被判处8年徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights the profound breach of trust when public officials betray their duties. Yahweh's word reminds us that faithfulness in small responsibilities reflects our character in larger ones. May we all strive for integrity in every role we are given, understanding that honesty builds trust and strengthens the fabric of society.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了公职人员背叛职责时对信任的严重破坏。雅伟的话语提醒我们，在小事上忠心的人，在大事上也忠心。愿我们都在所担任的每一个角色中追求正直，明白诚实能建立信任并巩固社会结构。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

title.en: Inspired by Ukraine, and worried by China: Taiwan teaches its citizens how to fly drones
title.zh: 受乌克兰启发，担忧中国大陆：台湾教导市民如何驾驶无人机

summary.en: Ordinary citizens in Taiwan are enrolling in drone piloting courses, inspired by events in Ukraine and concerned about a potential military threat from China. These courses teach participants, young and old, how to operate drones for various purposes.
summary.zh: 受乌克兰局势的启发并担忧中国大陆的军事威胁，台湾普通民众（包括年轻人和老年人）正在参加无人机驾驶课程。这些课程旨在教授学员如何操作无人机以应对潜在情况。

body.en: Ordinary Taiwanese, young and old, are joining courses to learn how to fly drones amid looming China military threat In a small, crowded room in Taipei, Pan Chien-chin is trying to keep a drone hovering steadily. Imagining himself flying a plane, he gently nudges controller joysticks to guide the insect-like device as it hums through the air. Cheers break out as Pan, who has never flown a drone before, steers it around a rectangular course marked by traffic cones without crashing. Around him are about two dozen fellow trainees, all signed up for the same course: Taiwan’s first civil defence drone training programme. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾普通民众，无论老少，都在参加课程，学习如何在迫在眉睫的中国军事威胁下驾驶无人机。在台北一间拥挤的小房间里，潘建钦正努力让无人机保持稳定盘旋。他想象自己驾驶一架飞机，轻轻推动控制器操纵杆，引导昆虫般的设备在空中嗡嗡作响。当潘以前从未驾驶过无人机时，他驾驶无人机绕着一个由交通锥标标记的矩形航线飞行，没有坠毁，引发了欢呼声。他周围大约有两打学员，他们都报名参加同一门课程：台湾首个民防无人机训练计划。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The story highlights a community's proactive response to perceived threats, reflecting a natural human inclination to prepare for potential dangers. Proverbs reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing trouble and taking steps to protect ourselves and our communities. Such foresight, when coupled with a reliance on Yahweh, can guide us in uncertain times.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻讲述了一个社区如何积极应对潜在威胁，反映了人类为可能出现的危险做准备的自然倾向。箴言提醒我们，预见祸患并采取措施保护自己和社区是智慧之举。这种远见，若能与对雅伟的信靠结合，便能在不确定的时期指引我们。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Lululemon apologises after Japanese drum row at Great Wall yoga event
title.zh: Lululemon因长城瑜伽活动中的日本太鼓风波致歉

summary.en: The activewear brand Lululemon issued an apology after an online uproar in China. The controversy stemmed from a promotional yoga event held on the Great Wall of China, where a Japanese taiko drum was mistakenly featured instead of a Chinese drum, despite the event being intended to celebrate Chinese culture.
summary.zh: 运动服饰品牌Lululemon因在中国长城举办的瑜伽推广活动中误用日本太鼓而引发网络争议后，发表了道歉声明。尽管该活动旨在庆祝中国文化，但这一失误在中国引发了线上轩然大波。

body.en: Online uproar follows Canadian brand’s use of taiko drum at sponsored festival held to celebrate Chinese culture The activewear brand Lululemon has apologised after a promotional event held on the Great Wall of China appeared to mistakenly feature a Japanese drum, prompting an uproar. The Canadian-headquartered company, known for its upmarket leggings, has been growing rapidly in China and arranged for a yoga festival to take place in late May on a section of the wall near Beijing. body.en: Indian fertility has fallen below the rate required for population stability, in further evidence of the unexpectedly rapid decline in births internationally The global fall in fertility rates has arrived faster and spread further than anticipated. Two-thirds of people now live in countries that have slipped below the replacement rate – 2.1 births per woman – required for a stable population. Last month, India revealed that its fertility rate had fallen to just 1.9 . The world’s two most populous nations, which pursued cruel and coercive policies to cut births, both face shrinking populations. China’s fertility rate is now around 1, and births last year fell below 8 million – just over half the number projected when the “one child” policy was axed 10 years ago, and comparable to the total in 1738, when its population was 150 million. It’s further proof that what was seen as a phenomenon of rich nations has spread far beyond them. East Asia led the way. title.en: US military plans major war stockpile on Australian soil
title.zh: 美国军方计划在澳大利亚建立大型战争储备

summary.en: The United States military is planning a significant accumulation of weapons on Australian territory. This move is described as a key part of an Asia-wide regional defense strategy aimed at countering the growing influence of China.
summary.zh: 美国军方正计划在澳大利亚领土上大量储备武器。此举被描述为一项旨在对抗中国崛起势力的亚洲区域防御战略的关键组成部分。

body.en:
The US military is planning a permanent war-ready weapons stockpile for its marine corps on Australia's southeast coast beyond the range of most Chinese missiles, tender documents show and officials confirmed to the Agence France-Presse news agency (AFP).

The development of the stockpile, a first for the US marine corps in Australia, comes as the United States is keen to leverage the continent's strategic location in the South Pacific to counter China's rapid military build-up, analysts said.

The US marine corps began global prepositioning of military supplies during the Cold War — using floating stores on ships and caves in Norway where weapons, ammunition and vehicles to sustain thousands of troops are kept.

The first land stockpile in the Asia-Pacific region is expected to open this year in the Philippines, close to potential flashpoints in the South China Sea.

Documents published by the US navy this month show advanced planning for an even larger Australian stockpile, with US$30 million ($42.4M) allocated to build warehouses and offices in southeastern Victoria state for "critical forward provisioning".

The Australian stockpile, expected to reach full capacity by 2028, will be kept in Melbourne before being moved to US warehouses to be constructed next year at an Australian military base at Bandiana in rural Victoria, tender documents show.

Australia does not permit foreign military bases on its soil, a sensitive issue in a country that has a security alliance with the United States and is hosting an increasing variety of US forces on rotation at Australian defence bases.

The US navy is engaging a global defence contractor to employ around 110 engineers, mechanics, material and safety specialists to manage the Australian stockpile, which includes "crew-served weapons", the documents show.

"Marine corps activities in Australia support integrated global sustainment by maintaining ready-for-issue equipment and supplies for operations and exercises across the Indo-Pacific," a US marine corps forces pacific spokesperson told AFP.

The spokesperson declined to comment on contract details or force planning assumptions but said marines' equipment is kept at "high readiness".

Contracting arrangements and the operation of the facility would be made in close coordination with Australia's Department of Defence.

"These activities improve responsiveness, strengthen interoperability with allies and partners, and support a range of missions across the Indo-Pacific," the spokesperson said, using an alternative description for the Asia-Pacific region.

title.en: Federal fuel tax discount extended, but not in full

summary.en: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he knew Australians were still "under pressure".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Cost relief at the bowser has been extended for another month, although the savings won't be as substantial.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has announced a limited extension of the fuel excise, making petrol and diesel 16 cents per litre cheaper than the full price in July.

The current saving is 32 cents a litre after it was cut three months ago, following the outbreak of war in the Middle East and ensuing strangulation of global oil supplies.

That discount is scheduled to expire on 30 June, by which time it will have cost the federal budget an estimated $2.9 billion in foregone revenue.

"(The) decision recognises that despite the welcome and substantial drop in the price of petrol recently, we know people are still under pressure," Mr Albanese said.

"Whether it's cutting the fuel tax, the road user charge for truckies or tax cuts for every taxpayer, we're taking action to ease pressure on Australians.

"We'll continue to do what we can to shield Australians from the worst impacts of this conflict including securing additional fuel from our partners."

The much anticipated confirmation of the ongoing albeit reduced saving coincides with a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and associated agreement between the United States and Iran to cease hostilities.

Iran's military said overnight it was going to close the strait again due to what it called ceasefire violations by Israel in Lebanon.

Australia currently has 44 days' worth of petrol in reserve, or about eight days more than when the US first bombed Iran in late February.

There are 51 tankers on the water and headed to Australia, with 3.9 billion litres of fuel contracted for delivery in the next month.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said he hoped the temporary support would still take some of the sting out of petrol prices and help with the cost of living.

"Despite the welcome and substantial drop in the price of petrol recently, we recognise people are still under pressure," he said.

"This extra month of fuel discount will help Australian motorists and businesses with the cost of living as this support tapers off."

The federal government confirmed on Saturday that the second week of June marked the highest level of fuel held in Australia since the minimum stock obligation came into force in 2023.

Drive through Yackandandah on a clear day, and you'll notice the rooftops before anything else. House after house topped with solar panels.

On the main street of this small tourist town in Victoria's north-east, Teslas and Nissan Leafs are parked outside the pie shop.

There's a community-owned electric vehicle charger around the corner, funded by the town's own petrol station. The postie delivers his mail on an electric bike. You might even spot a car driving around with a solar panel mounted on its roof.

For the residents of Yackandandah — or Yack, as most people call it — a future built on renewable energy isn't merely hypothetical. It's embedded in the town's DNA.

And it's part of a growing movement of communities across Australia experimenting with ways to cut power bills , improve energy reliability and reduce emissions.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In Yack, that effort has turned the town into an unlikely blueprint on how Australia might navigate the shift to renewable energy — not through major projects or government mandates, but through local ownership, community actions and decisions made around kitchen tables.

He lives in a house made of straw. While it sounds like something plucked from a fairy tale, his vision demonstrates what sustainable housing could look like.

"The beauty of straw is that it has really deep walls, so it's super insulative," Charles-Jones tells SBS News over a cup of peppermint tea in his home, whose thick, terracotta-coloured walls make it look cave-like.

"It's a waste product and ultimately it's organic, so it will eventually compost down. It lends itself well to unskilled builders. I'm not a builder at all. But it's quite forgiving."

Topped with solar panels, the house reflects a philosophy Charles-Jones would go on to spread across the town.

In 2014, he co-founded Totally Renewable Yackandandah (TRY), a community energy group, with a mission as straightforward as it sounds: get the whole town running on 100 per cent renewable energy , one rooftop at a time.

For Charles-Jones, the project was always about democratising energy from the ground up.

"You can do it at a very localised scale and get an immediate benefit from it," he says.

In 2002, the town bought its own petrol station after it was threatened with closure. Today, half of the profits go straight back into the community — providing grants to resurface netball courts, restore the local school's creek bed, buy the scouts a new trailer, and pay for the town's shiny new community-owned electric vehicle charger.

body.en:
Dane Waites lives with profound autism, a severe intellectual disability and bipolar disorder. His support plan was cut and he can no long afford key services

Christopher Knaus Sat 20 Jun 2026 16.00 EDT Last modified on Sat 20 Jun 2026 16.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Four months ago, Dane Waites sat down at his dining room table.

On a single piece of lined paper, pressed against a dark red tablecloth, he penned an urgent plea for help.

Waites was born with severe intellectual disability and received support through the National Disability Insurance Scheme .

He was sexually abused in the early 1990s at the Catholic-run Churinga Special Residential school, receiving compensation from St John of God in 2021 after suing the church.

Not long after receiving the settlement, the National Disability Insurance Agency informed Waites that the payout meant his NDIS funding would be slashed.

“The church awarded me money and written apology,” he wrote in his handwritten letter. “It was my abuse. [The judge] told me I got justice … goodbye bad man finished.

The agency applied a “compensation reduction amount”, a complex method used to prevent double-dipping by participants who receive court payouts that cover support services or equipment previously funded via the NDIS.

Waites lives with level three autism, the most profound form of autism spectrum disorder and has a severe intellectual disability and bipolar disorder. The confidential sum of compensation from the church was directly related to his abuse as a child, its continuing psychological and physical effects and the care and support he needs due to that abuse. The NDIS plan, which is not means tested, is designed to fund support services associated related to his permanent disability.

“You do not have to be Einstein to realise the Catholic church does not pay out for lifelong disabilities,” his mother, Junee Waites, 83, says.

“The compensation from the Catholic church did not come to Dane because of his disabilities.”

The Australian Lawyers Alliance has repeatedly advised government that survivors of historical child abuse matters should not be subject to compensation recovery or reduction as a matter of fairness.

“Victims of crime, victims of sexual abuse, victims of certain illnesses, such as asbestos-related illnesses … there’s many reasons why we would say that compensation recovery just doesn’t meet any fairness test at all,” Shaun Marcus, past ALA national president, said.

“Public policy should be that we exclude these types of claims from recovery, that’s the starting point. We would say a victim of child sexual abuse should not be subject [to compensation recovery], at all.”

body.zh: 戴恩·韦茨患有严重的自闭症、严重的智力障碍和躁郁症。他的支持计划被削减，他再也无法负担关键服务 Christopher Knaus 2026 年 6 月 20 日星期六 16:00 EDT 最后修改时间：2026 年 6 月 20 日星期六 16:01 EDT 分享 更喜欢 Google 上的卫报 四个月前，Dane Waites 坐在他的餐桌旁。 在一张压在深红色桌布上的横格纸上，他写下了紧急求助信。 韦茨出生时患有严重的智力残疾，并通过国家残疾保险计划获得支持。 1990 年代初，他在天主教开办的 Churinga 特殊寄宿学校遭受性虐待，并于 2021 年起诉教会后获得了圣约翰的赔偿。 收到和解协议后不久，国家残障保险局通知韦特斯，这笔赔偿意味着他的 NDIS 资金将被大幅削减。 “教会给了我钱并书面道歉，”他在手写信中写道。 “这是对我的虐待。[法官]告诉我，我得到了正义……再见，坏人结束了。 该机构采用了“补偿减少金额”，这是一种复杂的方法，用于防止收到法庭付款的参与者双重领取，这些付款涵盖了以前通过 NDIS 资助的支持服务或设备。 韦茨患有三级自闭症，这是自闭症谱系障碍中最严重的一种形式，并且患有严重的智力障碍和双相情感障碍。教会的保密赔偿金额与他童年时遭受的虐待、持续的心理和身体影响以及他因虐待而需要的照顾和支持直接相关。 NDIS 计划不进行经济情况调查，旨在资助与其永久残疾相关的支持服务。 “即使你不是爱因斯坦，也能意识到天主教会不会为终身残疾提供赔偿，”他 83 岁的母亲朱妮·韦茨 (Junee Waites) 说道。 “由于戴恩的残疾，天主教会的补偿没有降临到他身上。” 澳大利亚律师联盟多次建议政府，为了公平起见，历史性虐待儿童事件的幸存者不应获得赔偿或减少赔偿。 “犯罪受害者、性虐待受害者、某些疾病的受害者，例如与石棉相关的疾病……我们有很多理由说赔偿追回根本不符合任何公平标准，”前 ALA 全国主席肖恩·马库斯 (Shaun Marcus) 表示。 “公共政策应该是我们将这些类型的索赔排除在复苏之外，这是起点。我们想说，儿童性虐待的受害者根本不应该[获得赔偿]。” Waites 的计划去年削减了 25,000 美元，今年削减了 25,000 美元。他的支持人员这么说……

reflection.en: This story highlights the vulnerability of individuals like Dane, who rely on support systems and whose voices can easily be overlooked. Yahweh calls us to speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, ensuring justice for the poor and needy. Dane's mother's fight reminds us of the persistent advocacy required to protect the most vulnerable among us.
reflection.zh: 这个故事凸显了像戴恩这样依赖支持系统、声音容易被忽视的个体的脆弱性。雅伟呼召我们为那些无法为自己发声的人说话，确保穷人和困苦者得到公义。戴恩母亲的抗争提醒我们，保护我们当中最脆弱的人需要持续的倡导。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: After losing to the USA, can the Socceroos still get to the knockout rounds at World Cup?
title.zh: 澳大利亚国家足球队何去何从？

summary.en: After a crushing loss to the USA, the Socceroos will have one more shot to qualify for the next round.
summary.zh: 在惨败给美国队之后，澳大利亚国家足球队将有最后一次机会争取晋级下一轮。

body.en:
Socceroos and their fans around the world are reeling after a crushing loss to the USA on Saturday.

The shocking defeat began in the tenth minute with an own goal from Australia and ended with the Stars and Stripes closing in for a 2-0 win.

The result has sent Aussies careening back down to earth from the high pedestal set by the national team's 2-0 victory against Türkiye less than a week ago.

Socceroos coach Tony Popovic's selection decisions have come under scrutiny after the heartbreaking loss — Nestory Irankunda and Conor Metcalfe were benched in the opening half against the USA despite both players scoring against Türkiye in the team's opening match.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Popovic admitted the Socceroos looked "sluggish" and "heavy-legged" on Saturday, but said he didn't think the starting personnel would have made much of a difference against the USA's forceful performance.

"They were quicker, they were more powerful. They won every duel, they won every second ball, and when you do that, it makes it very difficult," he said.

But while humbling, it's far from the end for the Socceroos. Saturday's loss may mean the USA has topped Group D and will advance to the next round, the Group of 32, but Australia could still qualify with a second or third-place finish.

Saturday would prove consequential not only for Australia, but also for Türkiye, which became the second nation after Haiti to be eliminated from the 2026 World Cup after it was defeated by Paraguay 0-1. After this match, Paraguay levelled up to third place, where it is now equal with Australia on three points.

Australia will play Paraguay next week at 12pm on Friday, 26 June (AEST) at Santa Clara, near San Francisco, with the Socceroos needing just a win or a draw to progress automatically in second spot.

And automatic progression to the Group of 32 in second place would see Australia compete against another runner-up team, likely in Group G. In that group, the favourite pick to win is Belgium, while New Zealand, Iran and Egypt are battling for second place.

If Australia loses against Paraguay, it can still qualify for the Round of 32 as one of the best third-placed teams. This is because the top two teams from each group will advance to the Group of 32, along with the eight best third-place teams. A total of 32 teams will play in these knockout stages — you lose once, and you are out for good.

If the Socceroos made it to the Group of 32 under these conditions, their first match would be against a major group winner.

Paraguay's win cements the USA at the top of their group, a feat the team has only achieved twice, in 1930 and 2010....
body.zh: 周六惨败给美国队后，世界各地的澳大利亚足球队和他们的球迷都感到震惊。 这场令人震惊的失败始于澳大利亚队的乌龙球，比赛在第10分钟开始，最终星条旗队以2-0获胜。 这一结果让澳大利亚队从不到一周前国家队2-0战胜土耳其队所创下的高位上重新回到现实。 令人心碎的失利之后，澳大利亚队主教练托尼·波波维奇的选择决定受到了密切关注——内斯托里·伊兰昆达和康纳·梅特卡夫在对阵美国队的上半场比赛中被坐在替补席上，尽管两名球员在球队首场比赛中对阵土耳其队时都取得了进球。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 波波维奇承认澳大利亚队在周六看起来“迟缓”和“笨重”，但他表示，他认为首发阵容不会对美国队的强势表现产生太大影响。 “他们更快，更强大。他们赢得了每一场决斗，赢得了每一个球，当你这样做时，事情就会变得非常困难，”他说。 尽管令人羞愧，但澳大利亚队的结局还远未结束。周六的失利可能意味着美国已经在 D 组中排名第一，并将晋级下一轮 32 国集团，但澳大利亚仍可能以第二或第三名的成绩晋级。 周六的比赛不仅对澳大利亚，而且对土耳其也产生了重要影响。土耳其以 0-1 输给巴拉圭，成为继海地之后第二个在 2026 年世界杯上被淘汰的国家。本场比赛结束后，巴拉圭升至第三位，与澳大利亚同积3分。 澳大利亚将于下周 6 月 26 日星期五（澳大利亚东部标准时间）中午 12 点在旧金山附近的圣克拉拉对阵巴拉圭，澳大利亚队只需一场胜利或平局即可自动晋级第二名。 自动晋级 32 国集团第二名后，澳大利亚将与另一支亚军球队（很可能在 G 组）竞争。在该组中，最有希望获胜的球队是比利时，而新西兰、伊朗和埃及正在争夺第二名。 如果澳大利亚输给巴拉圭，它仍然可以作为最好的第三名球队之一晋级32强。这是因为每个小组的前两名球队将与八支成绩最好的第三名球队一起晋级32国小组。淘汰赛阶段共有 32 支球队进行比赛——输一次，就永远出局。 如果澳大利亚队在这种情况下进入 32 国集团，他们的第一场比赛将对阵主要小组冠军。 巴拉圭队的胜利巩固了美国队在小组中的领先地位，而该队仅在 1930 年和 2010 年两次实现过这一壮举......

reflection.en: The Socceroos' journey reminds us of the intense discipline and perseverance required in any pursuit, especially after a setback. Just as athletes train rigorously for a perishable crown, we are called to give our best in every endeavor, understanding that true reward lies beyond fleeting victories. This "one more shot" is an opportunity to demonstrate...
reflection.zh: 澳大利亚国家足球队的征程提醒我们，在任何追求中，尤其是在遭遇挫折之后，都需要严格的纪律和坚韧不拔的精神。正如运动员为那会朽坏的冠冕刻苦训练一样，我们也被呼召在每一次努力中尽力而为，明白真正的奖赏超越短暂的胜利。这“最后一次机会”是展现重新投入和希望的时刻。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

title.en: Police 'disappointed' following football fan chaos at watch events
title.zh: 警方对球迷观赛活动中的混乱表示“失望”

summary.en: Arrests were made at fan sites in both Sydney and Melbourne on Friday morning following incidents of disorder during football watch events, leading police to express disappointment.
summary.zh: 周五上午，悉尼和墨尔本的球迷观赛活动中发生骚乱，导致警方逮捕了一些人，并对此表示失望。

body.en:
Victorian police have said that flares and fireworks were "disappointingly" set off by football fans gathered at Federation Square for the Australia-United States match on Saturday morning.

Arrests were made at fan sites in the Victorian capital as well as Sydney's Tumbalong Park, where thousands of Socceroos fans packed in to watch the event in the early hours.

One man was treated at the scene in Sydney for facial burns after being hit in the face by a flare.

In Melbourne, mounted police were forced to intervene after fans attempted to breach barriers at Fed Square when the popular site reached capacity just after 4am on Saturday.

About 7,500 fans packed the site in cold and rainy conditions, with 14 flares and one firework set off before the match, leading to two arrests.

The pair will be charged on summons, with police reviewing CCTV to identify those responsible for setting off the remaining flares.

"Enforcing prohibited items such as flares from entering the live site remains the responsibility of the venue," a Victoria Police spokeswoman said.

A Fed Square spokesperson told SBS News that "while it was disappointing that this morning's match was marred by the actions of a small number of individuals, the overwhelming majority of attendees came together in great spirit to support the Socceroos".

Last month, Fed Square cancelled planned screenings of World Cup matches due to dangerous fan behaviour and the use of flares. That decision was overturned by Victorian Premier Jacinta Allen, who committed to increasing police presence at the site and enforcing a zero-tolerance approach to bad behaviour.

Fed Square said they would review Friday's operations with Victoria Police and apply any learnings to future screenings.

"We will continue working closely with police and other stakeholders to ensure the safest possible experience for everyone attending Federation Square," they said.

While fans celebrated the atmosphere, there was disappointment as the Socceroos' campaign suffered a setback with a 2-0 loss to the American team.

Former Socceroo Craig Foster, who was the MC at the live site, urged fans to stop letting off flares.

A 16-year-old boy was also arrested in relation to an alleged sexual assault of a woman about 4.55am.

Almost 9000 eager fans were redirected to AAMI Park, where the match was also livestreamed.

Sydney experienced similarly fiery scenes with two men, aged 20, arrested at Tumbarong Park in the city centre and later charged with possessing a bright light distress signal in a public place.

They were granted bail and are due to appear in court on Wednesday and police say investigations...

reflection.en: Even in moments of intense excitement, the call to self-control remains vital for maintaining public order and respect. The chaos witnessed at fan events reminds us that true passion is best expressed with discipline and consideration for others. Yahweh's spirit empowers us not for fear or disorder, but for power, love, and a sound mind.
reflection.zh: 即使在极度兴奋的时刻，自制力对于维护公共秩序和相互尊重仍然至关重要。球迷活动中出现的混乱提醒我们，真正的热情最好以纪律和对他人的体谅来表达。雅伟所赐的灵不是胆怯的，而是能力、仁爱和自律的灵。

verse.textEn: For the Spirit God gave us does not make us timid, but gives us power, love and self-discipline.
verse.textZh: 神赐给我们，不是胆怯的心，乃是刚强、仁爱、谨守的心。

title.en: Deadly H5 strain of bird flu has been confirmed in Australia — here's what it means
title.zh: 致命H5禽流感病毒株在澳大利亚确诊——这意味着什么

summary.en: Australia has confirmed its first case of the deadly H5N1 avian influenza, a significant development for the nation's public health.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚已确认首例致命H5N1禽流感病例，这对该国的公共卫生而言是一个重大进展。

body.en:
For years, as cases of the deadly H5 strain of bird influenza wreaked havoc among animal populations across the globe, Australia had been the sole continent to avoid it successfully — until now.

On Saturday, the first positive case of the virus on the Australian mainland was confirmed.

Agriculture minister Julie Collins confirmed at a press conference in Canberra that the H5 bird flu was detected in a migratory bird in Western Australia.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Australia will do all it can to curb any spread of H5N1 bird flu.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"There's no evidence of any mass mortalities, and there's no evidence that it's in our poultry or agriculture system at this stage," Collins added.

In its efforts to tackle previous bird-flu outbreaks, Australia has tightened biosecurity measures at farms, tested shore birds for disease, vaccinated vulnerable species, and war-gamed response plans for an H5N1 outbreak.

A single migratory wild seabird potentially infected with the disease was found in Western Australia on 14 June.

Before the suspected positive case was confirmed, Collins said on Friday that it would be "not unexpected" to discover.

"This will be sobering, but not unexpected given the spread globally," she said.

The bird was a brown skua — a sub-Antarctic species — that was found on a remote beach at the Cape Le Grand National Park near Esperance, about 700km southeast of Perth.

WA Agriculture and Food Minister Jackie Jarvis said the bird was isolated after it was discovered in an unwell state on Sunday and died that night.

"I'm told it is not normal for them to be on the south coast of Western Australia," Jarvis said.

"But I am also told it's not uncommon if a bird is sick to actually be sort of blown off course, as it were."

Initial tests were confirmed overnight by the CSIRO's Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness.

Senior lecturer at the Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies at the University of Tasmania, Dr Jane Younger, said the species infected with the virus could give clues to its origin.

"The species involved are important," she said, noting that they are Southern Ocean and sub-Antarctic birds.

This suggests that the virus "probably reached mainland Australia through Southern Ocean wildlife movements, rather than through the northern hemisphere route we have been watching closely," Younger explained.

But, she says, genetic analysis was still essential to identify the virus' origin and whether it was linked to current outbreaks across the Southern Ocean.

body.zh: 多年来，致命的 H5 禽流感病毒对全球动物种群造成了严重破坏，直到现在，澳大利亚一直是唯一成功避免感染的大陆。 周六，澳大利亚大陆确诊首例病毒阳性病例。 农业部长朱莉·柯林斯(Julie Collins)在堪培拉举行的新闻发布会上证实，西澳大利亚的一只候鸟中检测到H5禽流感。 总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯表示，澳大利亚将尽一切努力遏制 H5N1 禽流感的传播。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 柯林斯补充说：“没有证据表明存在任何大规模死亡，也没有证据表明现阶段我们的家禽或农业系统中存在这种情况。” 在应对之前的禽流感疫情的过程中，澳大利亚加强了农场的生物安全措施，对岸禽进行了疾病检测，对脆弱物种进行了疫苗接种，并针对 H5N1 疫情制定了应对计划。 6 月 14 日，在西澳大利亚发现了一只可能感染该疾病的迁徙野生海鸟。 在疑似阳性病例确诊之前，柯林斯周五表示，发现这一病例“并不意外”。 她说：“这将发人深省，但考虑到疫情在全球范围内的蔓延，这并不令人意外。” 这只鸟是一只棕色贼鸥——一种亚南极物种——是在珀斯东南约 700 公里埃斯佩兰斯附近勒格兰德角国家公园的一个偏远海滩上发现的。 西澳农业和食品部长杰基·贾维斯表示，这只鸟于周日被发现处于不适状态，并于当晚死亡，随后被隔离。 贾维斯说：“我听说他们出现在西澳大利亚州南海岸是不正常的。” “但我也被告知，如果一只鸟生病了，实际上被吹离了航线，这并不罕见。” 联邦科学与工业研究组织 (CSIRO) 的澳大利亚疾病预防中心连夜确认了初步测试结果。 塔斯马尼亚大学海洋和南极研究所的高级讲师简·杨格博士表示，感染该病毒的物种可以提供其起源的线索。 “所涉及的物种很重要，”她说，并指出它们是南大洋和亚南极地区的鸟类。 杨格尔解释说，这表明该病毒“可能通过南大洋野生动物的活动到达澳大利亚大陆，而不是通过我们一直密切关注的北半球路线”。 但是，她说，基因分析对于确定病毒的起源以及它是否与南大洋当前的疫情爆发有关仍然至关重要。 禽流感俗称禽流感，是一种主要影响鸟类的传染性病毒...

reflection.en: The confirmation of a deadly H5 bird flu strain reminds us of life's fragility and the constant presence of illness in our world. In such times, the Scriptures encourage us to pray for those affected by disease and for wisdom for those working to contain it. We can bring our concerns to Yahweh, trusting in His compassion and care.
reflection.zh: 致命H5禽流感病毒株的确认提醒我们生命的脆弱以及疾病在世上的持续存在。在这样的时刻，圣经鼓励我们为受疾病影响的人祷告，也为那些致力于控制疫情的人寻求智慧。我们可以将我们的担忧带到雅伟面前，信靠祂的怜悯和看顾。
